Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with reported head trauma and subsequent concussion
symptoms. Over the course of fifteen office visits, care consisted of sypmtom monitoring, cognitive and vestibular assessment,
graduated activity guidance, and periodic re-examination. The mechanism of injury described is consistent with the reported
concussion, and the clinical presentation is plausible for a crash of this type. Several examination findings, including balance and
oculomotor measures, support the diagnosis, while other neurological screening tests returned within normal limits. No prior
injury to the head or neck region is known to this provider. Treatment followed a typical course, with visit frequency decreasing
as symptoms improved and the patient progressed toward return to usual activities. Billed services are consistent with the
documented encounters, with no repeated or duplicate charges identified in the record.
